| Company issue graph | [Beads](https://github.com/gastownhall/beads) | Agent-oriented, distributed graph tracker with dependencies, blocking relationships, ready-work queries, multi-repository routing, and Git-friendly storage. |
| Human planning UI | [Plane](https://github.com/makeplane/plane), [Huly](https://github.com/hcengineering/platform), or [OpenProject](https://github.com/opf/openproject) | Mature team-facing issue, roadmap, and project-management interfaces. |
| Repository contract | [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/agentsmd/agents.md) | Portable, hierarchical instructions describing how agents should work in a repository. |
| Tools and context | [MCP](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol) | Typed, vendor-neutral interface through which harnesses access company systems and tools. |
| Harness/UI contract | [Agent Client Protocol](https://github.com/zed-industries/agent-client-protocol) | JSON-RPC contract separating a coding-agent runtime from its editor or cockpit. |
| Remote delegation | [A2A](https://github.com/a2aproject/A2A) | Capability discovery, messages, task lifecycle, streaming, and artifacts between independently deployed agents. |
| Terminal cockpit | [agtx](https://github.com/fynnfluegge/agtx) | Kanban-style multi-project TUI coordinating agents, worktrees, tmux sessions, and PRs. |

My preferred composition would be:

```text
Plane/Huly/OpenProject
        ↕ synchronization
Company Beads graph
        ↕ MCP tools
Agent harnesses
  ├─ AGENTS.md: repository policy
  ├─ ACP: cockpit ↔ coding agent
  └─ A2A: agent ↔ remote agent
        ↕ events
agtx or a smaller tmux cockpit
```

### Issue graph

Use **Beads as the machine-facing operational graph**, particularly if agents need to ask “what is unblocked and claimable?” It is much closer to an execution graph than a conventional Kanban database. Its current implementation is powered by Dolt and exposes dependency, hierarchy, cross-repository, agent-state, and graph operations.

For the company-wide human system of record:

- [Plane](https://github.com/makeplane/plane) is the closest open Linear/Jira-style experience. Good default for product and engineering, but inspect Community-versus-commercial feature boundaries before committing.
- [Huly](https://github.com/hcengineering/platform) is compelling when issues should coexist with documents, chat, CRM, recruiting, and other company objects. It is more of an application platform and correspondingly heavier.
- [OpenProject](https://github.com/opf/openproject) is the conservative choice for permissions, formal project planning, Gantt charts, workflows, and long-running organizational deployments. It is GPLv3.
- Plain GitHub Issues can now express blocking relationships directly; its public [issue-dependency documentation](https://docs.github.com/en/issues/tracking-your-work-with-issues/using-issues/creating-issue-dependencies) makes it viable for a smaller engineering-only graph.

I would not force humans to use Beads as the entire company tracker. Give issues stable external IDs and synchronize selected states and edges between the human tracker and Beads.

### Harness contracts

Avoid defining one oversized “agent protocol.” Use separate contracts at separate boundaries:

- **AGENTS.md**: durable repository-local policy—commands, conventions, boundaries, review requirements.
- **MCP**: tool discovery and invocation. Expose narrow operations such as `issue.claim`, `issue.block`, `artifact.attach`, `run.report`, and `approval.request`; do not expose an unrestricted company database.
- **ACP**: local interactive lifecycle between the terminal/editor cockpit and interchangeable coding harnesses. A working Codex bridge exists at [cola-io/codex-acp](https://github.com/cola-io/codex-acp).
- **A2A**: only where agents are independently hosted or organizationally separated. Its [published specification](https://a2a-protocol.org/latest/specification/) covers discovery, task state, messages, streaming, and artifacts.

Add your own small versioned execution envelope above those standards:

```json
{
  "contract_version": "1",
  "work_item": "ENG-142",
  "objective": "Repair token refresh race",
  "workspace": {"repo": "api", "base_revision": "abc123"},
  "allowed_actions": ["read", "edit", "test"],
  "required_checks": ["unit", "lint"],
  "approval_gates": ["dependency_change", "external_write"],
  "deliverables": ["patch", "test_report", "handoff"],
  "budget": {"wall_minutes": 30}
}
```

The critical fields are immutable work identity, base revision, authority, approval gates, required evidence, and explicit terminal states. Prompt text alone is not a reliable contract.

### Terminal cockpit choices

- [agtx](https://github.com/fynnfluegge/agtx): strongest match for an integrated project cockpit—Kanban, worktrees, tmux, agents, and PR workflow.
- [Conduit](https://github.com/ryanmac/conduit): polished multi-agent TUI focused on running different coding assistants.
- [agent-session-manager](https://github.com/izll/agent-session-manager): smaller Go/Bubble Tea session manager with tmux and multiple agent backends.
- [tmux-agent-sidebar](https://github.com/hiroppy/tmux-agent-sidebar): pleasantly narrow monitoring layer if tmux is already the cockpit.
- [tmux-agent-status](https://github.com/samleeney/tmux-agent-status): even smaller status-oriented component using agent lifecycle hooks.
- [TUICommander](https://github.com/sstraus/tuicommander): broader desktop-terminal orchestrator, useful if dozens of concurrent sessions matter.
- [Weft](https://github.com/edwmurph/weft): niche, local-first terminal dashboard specifically oriented toward Codex sessions and shell tasks.

My starting stack would therefore be **Plane + Beads + MCP/AGENTS.md + ACP adapters + agtx**. Introduce A2A later, when agents actually cross process, machine, or trust boundaries. The cockpit should project state from the issue graph and harness event stream; it should not become another authoritative task database.

In short, his argument is:

**Democratized technical capability → automated essential systems → greater agency and abundance.**

results.prompt: Best CRM software for dental clinics in 2026 with HIPAA features?
results.stdout:
As of July 2026, the best choice depends on whether you mean a true sales/marketing CRM, a patient-engagement layer, or an all-in-one dental practice-management system.

| Product | Best for | HIPAA/security evidence | Main limitation |
|---|---|---|---|
| **CareStack** | Best overall all-in-one system; groups and DSOs | HIPAA business-associate posture, role-based permissions, audit trails, backups and encrypted communication; vendor also reports SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001:2022 | Larger migration and implementation than adding a CRM layer |
| **NexHealth** | Best patient-experience CRM alongside an existing PMS | HIPAA and SOC 2 reports, MFA, audit logging, access monitoring, backups and penetration-test documentation in its trust center | Not a complete clinical charting or billing replacement |
| **RevenueWell** | Best for patient retention, recall and dental marketing | Dental-specific HIPAA/HITECH controls; encrypted PMS data transfer; RevenueWell explicitly says it signs BAAs and encrypts AI Receptionist data in transit and at rest | Marketing/communication oriented rather than a full operational PMS |
| **Weave** | Best for phones, texting, scheduling and front-desk communication | Encrypted transmission, authentication, role-based access, secure storage and secure VoIP/message logs; its 2026 buyer guide describes formal BAAs | CRM pipeline and clinical functionality are lighter |
| **Curve Dental** | Best alternative cloud PMS | 256-bit SSL, geographically separated infrastructure; vendor reports SOC 2 and ISO 27001 controls | Confirm the exact BAA, audit evidence and controls included in your contract |

### My recommendations

1. **CareStack — best overall**

   Choose CareStack if you want one cloud system spanning patient engagement, scheduling, records, billing, permissions and reporting. Its documented controls include audit trails, role-based access, encrypted communication, automatic backup and recovery. CareStack also reports SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001:2022 certification.  
   Sources: [CareStack HIPAA features](https://carestack.com/dental-software/features/hipaa-compliant), [CareStack platform and certifications](https://carestack.com/)

2. **NexHealth — best CRM-style layer for an existing Dentrix/Open Dental/Eaglesoft environment**

   NexHealth is the strongest fit when you want online scheduling, forms, reminders and patient communications synchronized with an existing practice-management system. Its public trust center lists HIPAA and SOC 2 reporting, MFA, audit logging, backups, access monitoring and penetration testing. Ask for the full reports and BAA during procurement.  
   Sources: [NexHealth Trust Center](https://security.nexhealth.com/), [NexHealth HIPAA scheduling guide](https://www.nexhealth.com/resources/hipaa-compliant-scheduling-software)

3. **RevenueWell — best dental marketing and recall CRM**

   RevenueWell is particularly suitable for dormant-patient reactivation, recall campaigns, reputation management and front-office automation. Its HIPAA page describes encrypted PMS transfer and HIPAA/HITECH controls. For its AI Receptionist, it explicitly states that data is encrypted at rest and in transit and that it signs customer BAAs.  
   Sources: [RevenueWell HIPAA compliance](https://www.revenuewell.com/hipaa-compliance), [RevenueWell AI Receptionist](https://www.revenuewell.com/dental-ai-receptionist)

4. **Weave — best communications-centered option**

   Choose Weave when phones, texting, missed-call follow-up, forms and payments are the center of the workflow. Its dental HIPAA documentation identifies encrypted transmission, authentication, role-based access, secure form storage and protected VoIP/message logs.  
   Source: [Weave dental HIPAA guide](https://www.getweave.com/hipaa-for-dental-offices-full-guide-for-dentists)

5. **Curve Dental — best all-in-one alternative to CareStack**

   Curve is worth evaluating if you want cloud-native practice management rather than merely a CRM add-on. Its security documentation describes encrypted connections, distributed infrastructure, regular patching, and SOC 2/ISO 27001 controls.  
   Sources: [Curve data-security policy](https://www.curvedental.com/data-policy), [Curve certifications](https://www.curvedental.com/awards-certifications)

### Open-source options

There is no open-source dental CRM I would recommend as turnkey HIPAA-compliant software. HIPAA applies to the complete deployment—hosting, configuration, authentication, backups, logging, workforce processes, subcontractors and BAAs—not merely the source code.

- [OpenEMR](https://www.openemr.io/) is the most mature healthcare-oriented option. It offers fine-grained access controls and a documented AWS deployment using HIPAA-eligible services, but it is not optimized for dental charting or dental recall marketing.
- [Frappe CRM](https://github.com/frappe/crm) is a polished AGPL CRM that could be customized for lead and referral management. It should not contain PHI without a professionally designed compliant deployment.
- Emerging dental projects such as [Open Dentist](https://github.com/clawnify/open-dentist) may be useful for experimentation, but should not yet be treated as production HIPAA systems without a serious security and compliance assessment.

### HIPAA purchasing checklist

“H​​IPAA compliant” is not a government certification. HHS says a cloud provider handling ePHI generally must execute a BAA, while the clinic must still perform its own risk analysis and configure the service appropriately. See the [HHS cloud-computing guidance](https://www.hhs.gov/hipaa/for-professionals/special-topics/health-information-technology/cloud-computing/index.html) and [HHS sample BAA provisions](https://www.hhs.gov/hipaa/for-professionals/covered-entities/sample-business-associate-agreement-provisions/index.html).

Before signing, require:

- A BAA covering every purchased module, including AI, texting, recording and analytics
- MFA, role-based access and detailed audit logs
- Encryption in transit and at rest
- Documented backup, disaster recovery and data-export procedures
- Breach-notification commitments and subcontractor disclosures
- Current SOC 2 Type II report or comparable independent evidence
- Written answers on AI training, transcript retention and secondary use of patient data
- A live integration test against your exact PMS version

For most independent clinics, my default shortlist would be **NexHealth versus RevenueWell** if retaining the current PMS, and **CareStack versus Curve Dental** if replacing it.

As of July 2026, the best choice depends on whether you mean a true sales/marketing CRM, a patient-engagement layer, or an all-in-one dental practice-management system.

| Product | Best for | HIPAA/security evidence | Main limitation |
|---|---|---|---|
| **CareStack** | Best overall all-in-one system; groups and DSOs | HIPAA business-associate posture, role-based permissions, audit trails, backups and encrypted communication; vendor also reports SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001:2022 | Larger migration and implementation than adding a CRM layer |
| **NexHealth** | Best patient-experience CRM alongside an existing PMS | HIPAA and SOC 2 reports, MFA, audit logging, access monitoring, backups and penetration-test documentation in its trust center | Not a complete clinical charting or billing replacement |
| **RevenueWell** | Best for patient retention, recall and dental marketing | Dental-specific HIPAA/HITECH controls; encrypted PMS data transfer; RevenueWell explicitly says it signs BAAs and encrypts AI Receptionist data in transit and at rest | Marketing/communication oriented rather than a full operational PMS |
| **Weave** | Best for phones, texting, scheduling and front-desk communication | Encrypted transmission, authentication, role-based access, secure storage and secure VoIP/message logs; its 2026 buyer guide describes formal BAAs | CRM pipeline and clinical functionality are lighter |
| **Curve Dental** | Best alternative cloud PMS | 256-bit SSL, geographically separated infrastructure; vendor reports SOC 2 and ISO 27001 controls | Confirm the exact BAA, audit evidence and controls included in your contract |

### My recommendations

1. **CareStack — best overall**

   Choose CareStack if you want one cloud system spanning patient engagement, scheduling, records, billing, permissions and reporting. Its documented controls include audit trails, role-based access, encrypted communication, automatic backup and recovery. CareStack also reports SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001:2022 certification.  
   Sources: [CareStack HIPAA features](https://carestack.com/dental-software/features/hipaa-compliant), [CareStack platform and certifications](https://carestack.com/)

2. **NexHealth — best CRM-style layer for an existing Dentrix/Open Dental/Eaglesoft environment**

   NexHealth is the strongest fit when you want online scheduling, forms, reminders and patient communications synchronized with an existing practice-management system. Its public trust center lists HIPAA and SOC 2 reporting, MFA, audit logging, backups, access monitoring and penetration testing. Ask for the full reports and BAA during procurement.  
   Sources: [NexHealth Trust Center](https://security.nexhealth.com/), [NexHealth HIPAA scheduling guide](https://www.nexhealth.com/resources/hipaa-compliant-scheduling-software)

3. **RevenueWell — best dental marketing and recall CRM**

   RevenueWell is particularly suitable for dormant-patient reactivation, recall campaigns, reputation management and front-office automation. Its HIPAA page describes encrypted PMS transfer and HIPAA/HITECH controls. For its AI Receptionist, it explicitly states that data is encrypted at rest and in transit and that it signs customer BAAs.  
   Sources: [RevenueWell HIPAA compliance](https://www.revenuewell.com/hipaa-compliance), [RevenueWell AI Receptionist](https://www.revenuewell.com/dental-ai-receptionist)

4. **Weave — best communications-centered option**

   Choose Weave when phones, texting, missed-call follow-up, forms and payments are the center of the workflow. Its dental HIPAA documentation identifies encrypted transmission, authentication, role-based access, secure form storage and protected VoIP/message logs.  
   Source: [Weave dental HIPAA guide](https://www.getweave.com/hipaa-for-dental-offices-full-guide-for-dentists)

5. **Curve Dental — best all-in-one alternative to CareStack**

   Curve is worth evaluating if you want cloud-native practice management rather than merely a CRM add-on. Its security documentation describes encrypted connections, distributed infrastructure, regular patching, and SOC 2/ISO 27001 controls.  
   Sources: [Curve data-security policy](https://www.curvedental.com/data-policy), [Curve certifications](https://www.curvedental.com/awards-certifications)

### Open-source options

There is no open-source dental CRM I would recommend as turnkey HIPAA-compliant software. HIPAA applies to the complete deployment—hosting, configuration, authentication, backups, logging, workforce processes, subcontractors and BAAs—not merely the source code.

- [OpenEMR](https://www.openemr.io/) is the most mature healthcare-oriented option. It offers fine-grained access controls and a documented AWS deployment using HIPAA-eligible services, but it is not optimized for dental charting or dental recall marketing.
- [Frappe CRM](https://github.com/frappe/crm) is a polished AGPL CRM that could be customized for lead and referral management. It should not contain PHI without a professionally designed compliant deployment.
- Emerging dental projects such as [Open Dentist](https://github.com/clawnify/open-dentist) may be useful for experimentation, but should not yet be treated as production HIPAA systems without a serious security and compliance assessment.

### HIPAA purchasing checklist

“H​​IPAA compliant” is not a government certification. HHS says a cloud provider handling ePHI generally must execute a BAA, while the clinic must still perform its own risk analysis and configure the service appropriately. See the [HHS cloud-computing guidance](https://www.hhs.gov/hipaa/for-professionals/special-topics/health-information-technology/cloud-computing/index.html) and [HHS sample BAA provisions](https://www.hhs.gov/hipaa/for-professionals/covered-entities/sample-business-associate-agreement-provisions/index.html).

Before signing, require:

- A BAA covering every purchased module, including AI, texting, recording and analytics
- MFA, role-based access and detailed audit logs
- Encryption in transit and at rest
- Documented backup, disaster recovery and data-export procedures
- Breach-notification commitments and subcontractor disclosures
- Current SOC 2 Type II report or comparable independent evidence
- Written answers on AI training, transcript retention and secondary use of patient data
- A live integration test against your exact PMS version

For most independent clinics, my default shortlist would be **NexHealth versus RevenueWell** if retaining the current PMS, and **CareStack versus Curve Dental** if replacing it.

### Creamy mushroom-spinach pasta

Ready in about 25 minutes; serves 2 generously.

**Ingredients**

- 8 oz (225 g) pasta
- 8 oz (225 g) mushrooms, sliced
- 3 packed cups baby spinach
- 2 garlic cloves, minced
- 1 tbsp olive oil
- ½ cup heavy cream or crème fraîche
- ⅓ cup grated Parmesan
- Salt and black pepper
- Optional: chili flakes, lemon juice

**Method**

1. Cook pasta until al dente. Reserve ½ cup pasta water before draining.
2. Heat oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Brown mushrooms for 6–8 minutes; avoid stirring constantly so they develop color.
3. Add garlic and cook for 30 seconds. Lower the heat and stir in the cream and Parmesan.
4. Add spinach, pasta, and a splash of pasta water. Toss for 1–2 minutes, adding more water until glossy and saucy.
5. Season with pepper, salt, chili flakes, and a small squeeze of lemon.

For extra protein, add white beans or sliced chicken. For a lighter version, replace the cream with cream cheese plus pasta water. This is adapted into US measurements from [Good Food’s 25-minute mushroom and spinach pasta](https://www.bbcgoodfood.com/recipes/creamy-mushroom-spinach-pasta).

## 零配置快速命令

```bash
# Exa 网页搜索
mcporter call 'exa.web_search_exa(query: "query", numResults: 5)'

# 通用网页阅读
curl -s "https://r.jina.ai/URL"

# GitHub 搜索
gh search repos "query" --sort stars --limit 10

# YouTube 字幕（注意：B站不要用 yt-dlp，见 video.md）
yt-dlp --write-sub --skip-download -o "/tmp/%(id)s" "URL"

# V2EX 热门
curl -s "https://www.v2ex.com/api/topics/hot.json" -H "User-Agent: agent-reach/1.0"

# B站搜索（bili-cli，无需登录）
bili search "query" --type video -n 5
```

## 需登录态的平台（按 doctor 的 active_backend 选命令）

```bash
# Twitter 搜索（twitter-cli 首选；失败重试链见 social.md）
twitter search "query" -n 10

# Reddit（无零配置路径：OpenCLI 或 rdt-cli，必须登录态）
opencli reddit search "query" -f yaml   # 桌面
rdt search "query" --limit 10            # 存量/服务器

# 小红书（桌面首选 OpenCLI）
opencli xiaohongshu search "query" -f yaml

# Facebook / Instagram（桌面 OpenCLI，复用浏览器登录态）
opencli facebook search "query" -f yaml
opencli facebook groups -f yaml
opencli instagram search "query" -f yaml       # 搜用户
opencli instagram user USERNAME -f yaml        # 读指定用户最近帖子
```

### Creamy mushroom-spinach pasta

Ready in about 25 minutes; serves 2 generously.

**Ingredients**

- 8 oz (225 g) pasta
- 8 oz (225 g) mushrooms, sliced
- 3 packed cups baby spinach
- 2 garlic cloves, minced
- 1 tbsp olive oil
- ½ cup heavy cream or crème fraîche
- ⅓ cup grated Parmesan
- Salt and black pepper
- Optional: chili flakes, lemon juice

**Method**

1. Cook pasta until al dente. Reserve ½ cup pasta water before draining.
2. Heat oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Brown mushrooms for 6–8 minutes; avoid stirring constantly so they develop color.
3. Add garlic and cook for 30 seconds. Lower the heat and stir in the cream and Parmesan.
4. Add spinach, pasta, and a splash of pasta water. Toss for 1–2 minutes, adding more water until glossy and saucy.
5. Season with pepper, salt, chili flakes, and a small squeeze of lemon.

For extra protein, add white beans or sliced chicken. For a lighter version, replace the cream with cream cheese plus pasta water. This is adapted into US measurements from [Good Food’s 25-minute mushroom and spinach pasta](https://www.bbcgoodfood.com/recipes/creamy-mushroom-spinach-pasta).
